subject.title: Fork-per-issue from one warmed repo box

question: Should Clownfish adopt a snapshot-forked warmed repository workspace backend, and if so what isolation, cache, credential, and fallback contract must it guarantee?
rationale: Current work provides adjacent checkout and concurrency mechanisms but does not determine whether a new runtime dependency and lifecycle model fit the project’s operational boundary.

options.title: Design an opt-in warmed backend
options.body: Sponsor a short architecture design that defines the snapshot provider, isolation guarantees, cleanup, observability, fallback to fresh clones, and a staged opt-in rollout before implementation.

options.title: Keep fresh-clone execution
options.body: Retain the current isolated checkout model and close the proposal only if maintainers decide the operating-cost savings do not justify a new workspace backend.

options.title: Prototype outside the default path
options.body: Run a non-default proof of concept against representative repository workloads and return with measured setup savings and isolation evidence before committing to a core integration.

recommendation.title: Design an opt-in warmed backend
recommendation.body: Sponsor a short architecture design that defines the snapshot provider, isolation guarantees, cleanup, observability, fallback to fresh clones, and a staged opt-in rollout before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work is the strongest available history signal for the existing worker checkout and concurrency paths that a warmed backend would extend.
